# fal raises serverless H100 rate to $2.49/hr, adds GB200 GPU, doubles MiniMax video pricing

By Rob Litterst, Co-founder, PricingSaaS

Published Oct 2, 2026

## What changed

fal's serverless GPU pricing moved across the board: H100 instances rose from $1.89 to $2.49 per hour (up 32%), B300 instances rose from $4.49 to $5.99 per hour (up 33%), and a new GB200 GPU tier was added to the lineup. Separately, MiniMax's H3 Max video model saw its per-second generation rate double, from $0.025 to $0.05.

## Why it matters

For teams building on fal, this is a direct cost-of-goods increase on two of its most-used GPU tiers plus a 2x jump on one of its video models - margin that has to be absorbed or passed through to end customers. For fal, layering in GB200 support signals it's racing to keep pace with Nvidia's newest hardware generation while monetizing the older fleet harder. Watch whether this is the start of a broader repricing across fal's remaining GPU and model catalog, given it's now made three pricing moves in ten weeks, or whether this settles back into the roughly 30-day cadence its track record shows.

## In context

This is fal's third real pricing change since tracking began in late July — coming just a day after it finished filling out its Audio and 3D model API price lists on Oct 1 — and its second GPU rate hike since the H100 list price moved to $4.50/hr in early August. Price increases are everywhere in the index right now: Shipday's Enterprise tier jumped 40%, Cumul raised its USD plan 25%, and Hedra hiked its Individual plan all landed in the same late-September window. Most of those are SaaS seat pricing; fal's move extends the same pressure to raw GPU-hour and per-second inference rates, the cost layer underneath everyone else's AI pricing.

### GPU Hourly Rates Compared

If you rent GPUs directly, this is the table that matters. fal.ai shows a list price and a lower "as low as" price. Replicate shows one public rate.

| GPU | fal.ai list | fal.ai lowest shown | Replicate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | $4.50/hr | $2.49/hr | $5.49/hr |
| H200 (141GB) | $6.00/hr | $2.99/hr | Check live page |
| B200 (192GB) | $7.99/hr | $5.49/hr | Not listed |
| A100 (80GB) | Not on pricing page | Not on pricing page | $5.04/hr |
| L40S | Not on pricing page | Not on pricing page | $3.51/hr |
| T4 | Not on pricing page | Not on pricing page | $0.81/hr |

At list price, the H100 gap is $0.99 per hour. The lower fal.ai figures are best-case rates, and the page sends larger buyers to sales for them. Some third-party roundups still quote an H100 at around $1.89 per hour on fal.ai, which does not match the pricing page today, so ignore older numbers.

Worked example: 100 H100 hours cost $450 on fal.ai at list price, $549 on Replicate, and $249 at fal.ai's lowest shown rate. That is a $99 difference at list and a $300 difference at the best rate.

...

### Break-Even Math for Dedicated GPUs

The question is how many images an hour a dedicated GPU must produce to beat pay-per-output pricing. Divide the hourly GPU price by the price of one image:

| Model price | GPU at $5.49/hr | GPU at $4.50/hr |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FLUX Dev at $0.025 | 220 images per hour | 180 images per hour |
| FLUX Schnell at $0.003 | 1,830 images per hour | 1,500 images per hour |

Below those volumes, you pay less by buying outputs. Above them, a busy dedicated GPU starts to win, but only if it stays busy around the clock. At 180 images an hour you need one image every 20 seconds, nonstop, with no gaps for nights or weekends. Most small products never reach that, which is why pay-per-output is the safer default.

results.title: fal.ai Pricing: API Costs, Free Credits and MCP
results.author: Cristian Da Conceicao
highlights:
The short version: fal.ai is prepaid and billed per output. Images run from $0.003 per megapixel up to $0.15 per image, video from a few cents to $0.40 per second, GPUs rent by the hour, and the MCP server itself is free. You pay only for the runs it triggers, at the same rates as a direct API call.

...

fal runs on a prepaid credit model. Its terms say you buy credits in advance, and every run, through the web interface or an API call, deducts its cost from your balance. What you are charged per depends on what the model makes:

| Output | Billing unit | Example from the pricing page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Images | Per image or per megapixel | $0.0398 per image (Nano Banana) |
| Video | Per second, or per video | $0.14 per second (Kling Video v3) |
| Language and other models | Per request or per compute second | Varies by model |
| Raw compute | Per GPU hour | $2.49 to $4.50 for an H100 |

Think of it as a utility meter, not a subscription. Nothing runs, nothing is charged. fal's own wording is that you only pay for the computing power you consume, and the docs add that you pay for successful outputs, never for time spent waiting in the queue.

...

## GPU Hourly Rates

When no hosted model fits, fal rents GPUs by the hour. The pricing page shows a range for each card:

| GPU | Memory | Hourly rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $1.99 to $4.00 |
| H100 | 80 GB | $2.49 to $4.50 |
| H200 | 141 GB | $2.99 to $6.00 |
| B200 | 192 GB | $5.49 to $7.99 |
| GB200 | 192 GB | $5.89 to $9.99 |
| B300 | 288 GB | $5.99 to $12.99 |

An 8 hour job on one H100 costs between $19.92 and $36. Leave that same card running around the clock for a 730 hour month and the bill is $1,817.70 at the low end and $3,285 at the high end.

Compare that with per-run pricing. On price alone, an always-on H100 at $2.49 per hour only beats FLUX.1 schnell at $0.003 per image once you pass roughly 600,000 one-megapixel images a month. Below that, per-run billing wins, and it needs no one watching an idle machine.

results.title: fal doubles Flux 3 Image edit price to $0.048 per megapixel — PricingSaaS Pulse
results.author: Rob Litterst
highlights:
## What changed

fal's Flux 3 Image edit endpoint (blackforestlabs/flux-3/edit-image) rose from $0.024 to $0.048 per megapixel, a 100% increase, cutting the units-per-$1 rate from 41.67 to 20.83 megapixels. No other row on the Image models table moved.

## Why it matters

For teams building against Flux 3 Image, a price that doubles within a week of launch is a reminder that newly introduced endpoints are the least stable line items on fal's rate card. Watch whether other recently added models get repriced on a similar timeline.

## In context

fal has made 5 pricing changes in the last 90 days, averaging one every 19 days. It published Audio and 3D model pricing on Oct 1, raised its H100 GPU rate to $2.49/hr and doubled MiniMax video pricing on Oct 2, and introduced Flux 3 Image editing at $0.024 per megapixel on Oct 9. Its earlier tracked price increase was an Aug 3 hike to its H100 GPU list price, from $3.99 to $4.50 per hour. What's new here is repricing a model within a week of listing it.

results.author: reAPI Team
highlights:
## En bref

- Les tarifs Fal AI sont fixés par modèle. Seedance 2.5 est affiché à environ $0.2205, $0.4730 et $1.164 par seconde en 480p, 720p et 1080p ; Nano Banana Pro à $0.15 par image, doublé en 4K [1].
- Les mêmes modèles sont affichés de 16% à 90% moins cher sur reAPI, avec les plus grands écarts sur Nano Banana Pro et Nano Banana 2 [1] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8].
- Les crédits gratuits de fal prennent la forme de dotations et de coupons, valables entre une semaine et un an ; les crédits achetés expirent après 365 jours [2].
- fal ne facture pas les erreurs serveur, mais une erreur côté client comme HTTP 422 peut tout de même être facturée si du temps GPU a déjà été consommé [2].
- Les nouveaux comptes fal traitent 2 requêtes à la fois, limite qui monte automatiquement jusqu'à 40 à mesure que vous achetez des crédits [2].

## Comment fonctionne la tarification de fal AI

fal.ai vend deux choses : des API de modèles hébergés et des GPU serverless pour vos propres déploiements. Les API de modèles sont facturées par résultat, soit par image, soit par seconde de vidéo générée, et certains modèles publient aussi une formule en tokens derrière le chiffre par seconde. Le temps GPU pour les déploiements personnalisés relève d'un tarif horaire distinct, affiché à partir de $2.49 de l'heure pour un H100 [1] [3].

Trois règles de la FAQ de fal comptent pour la facture. Le temps de démarrage à froid n'est pas facturé sur les endpoints Model API, seul le temps d'inférence l'est. Les erreurs serveur (HTTP 500 et au-delà) ne sont jamais facturées. Les erreurs côté client, comme des entrées invalides (HTTP 422), peuvent quand même être facturées si un runner a consommé du temps GPU sur la requête avant que l'erreur ne soit détectée [2]. Si votre pipeline envoie beaucoup de requêtes mal formées, c'est de cette dernière règle que viennent les coûts inattendus.

results.title: a16z chart: GPU rental prices hold firm while token ...
highlights:
# a16z chart: GPU rental prices hold firm while token prices fall, a Jevons-style pattern

Nathan LeClaire flagged an a16z Growth chart, compiled by Citadel Securities from Ornn, Silicon Data and Bloomberg data as of August 2026, that tracks the H100 GPU rental price against a token-price expenditure index. In late spring the two moved down together, but from July token prices kept falling, with the index dropping from roughly 1.6 to about 1.0, while the H100 rental price stayed at around $2.7 an hour. The chart is titled "Jevons: Compute Prices Rise As Token Prices Fall": cheaper tokens appear to be lifting demand for compute rather than easing it. Theo (t3.gg) quote-posted it with the comment "Called it".

results.title: How To Do Motion Design Video Generation With Claude ...
results.author: John Ozuysal
highlights:
In a Claude chat with the fal connector switched on, Claude Opus 5.5 can generate keyframes on fal and hand the motion between them to MiniMax H3 Max reference-to-video, with nothing to install. Claude generates the frames each shot has to hit, and H3 Max generates the motion that connects them. When a shot opens on the exact frame the previous one landed on, the join has no hard cut, and the three shots play as one continuous take, for about $2.05 to $2.17 at fal's standard rates.

...

The walkthrough comes to between $2.05 and $2.17 at our standard rates before retries, depending on whether the opening and landing keyframes count as reference images.

Three five-second 9:16 shots at 768P on MiniMax H3 Max reference-to-video account for $1.20 to $1.28 of that.

H3 Max reference-to-video output is priced per second of requested duration: $0.05 at 480P, $0.08 at 768P and $0.16 at 1080P.

Above the 4,096 reference tokens included in each request, extra tokens cost $0.02 per 1,000, prorated.

A 9:16 reference image counts as 1,824 tokens, so the product photo on its own stays inside the allowance.

With the opening and landing keyframes counted as well, a shot carries 5,472 reference tokens, and the 1,376 tokens above the allowance add about $0.03.

results.title: Compute Capacity Acquisition at Fal: $200K–$250K | The AI Wins
highlights:
### About this role:

You'll make sure fal can get the GPUs it needs, at the right price, the moment it needs them. You'll own fal's relationships with hyperscalers and neoclouds, know what capacity exists and what it really costs, and bring the best of it to the table.

This is a technical and commercial role in equal parts. You'll judge a supplier's offer from the GPU up to the data center, negotiate terms alongside our deal team, and hold a clear view of where the compute market is heading. It is not a sales role, and it is not a procurement desk.

### What you’ll do

- Supplier relationships. Build deep, multi-level relationships across hyperscalers and neoclouds, including NVIDIA cloud partners, so fal is the first call when capacity frees up.
- Capacity evaluation. Assess every offer from the GPU to the data center: hardware generation, node and rack configuration, interconnect, power density and cooling. Know what a configuration will actually deliver, not just what the spec sheet says.
- Pricing and market intelligence. Track rates by GPU generation, region and contract term. Explain why a price moved, what it signals, and when fal should buy, wait or switch.
- Negotiation. Work with our deal team to negotiate capacity commitments, deposits and payment timing, SLAs and remedies, and carry agreements to signature.
- Sourcing against fal's needs. Turn GPU requirements from our fleet operations team and demand forecasts into a sourcing plan: which suppliers, which regions, which terms.
- Market point of view. Form and defend a view on supply coming online, platform transitions such as new GPU generations, and regional or policy shifts. Turn it into concrete sourcing decisions.
